sections.title: Domain 1: Foundation Model Integration, Data Management, and Compliance

keyTerms.definition: The AWS exam for generative AI applications on AWS, with 75 total questions, 65 scored, and a 750 out of 1000 passing score.
Foundation Model Integration, Data Management, and Compliance, the exam's center of gravity at 31 percent of the score.

recall.question: What share of the AIP-C01 exam is Domain 1?
recall.answer: Domain 1 is 31 percent of the score, roughly 20 scored questions.

recall.question: What single question does Domain 1 answer?
recall.answer: How to get the correct model, the correct data, and the correct controls into a working system on AWS.

sections.title: How to use this volume

keyTerms.definition: The approach ladder: prompt engineering, then RAG, then agents, then fine-tuning, stopping at the cheapest step that works.
The exam's preferred style: choose the option with the least operational overhead.

recall.question: What is the recommended way to read this volume?
recall.answer: Read a topic, then do its drill questions at the end, which are written in the exam's choose the MOST correct answer style.

recall.question: What are the three ideas that run through the whole domain?
recall.answer: Climb the ladder in order and stop at the cheapest step that works, prefer managed and serverless, and map each scenario constraint to one decision.

sections.title: 1. Foundation models on Bedrock

keyTerms.definition: A large AI model pre-trained on broad data that you call through an API instead of training yourself.
Running the model on your input to produce an output, which is what every API call in this volume is.
The limit on how much text a model can consider per request, counted in tokens.
The fully managed AWS service for calling foundation models from many providers through one set of AWS APIs.
The control that reshapes token probabilities, where 0 is deterministic and higher values are more creative.

recall.question: Why does the exam's most correct architecture almost always route through Bedrock?
recall.answer: Bedrock gives one front door to many models with one IAM authentication model and one CloudTrail audit trail, instead of per-vendor APIs or self-hosted endpoints.

recall.question: What usually causes an AccessDeniedException on a Bedrock model call?
recall.answer: Model access was never requested for that model in that region, or the model is not available in that region. It does not mean the IAM policy is wrong.

recall.question: What are the three controls that shape which token the model picks?
recall.answer: Temperature, top-p nucleus sampling, and max tokens. Temperature 0 is deterministic and correct for classification and extraction.

sections.title: 2. Choosing the right model

keyTerms.definition: The model selection trade-off: capability, cost per token, latency, context window, and regional availability.
A fixed set of question-answer pairs used as a quality benchmark to test candidate models.
The first selection filter: drop any model below the quality bar on your golden dataset.
A design that routes easy requests to a cheap model and escalates only hard ones to the flagship.

recall.question: What is the correct model-selection filter order?
recall.answer: Capability floor on a golden dataset, regional availability, cost and latency ranking, then context window check. The cheapest model that meets every requirement wins.

recall.question: What is the 'bigger is safer' trap?
recall.answer: Defaulting to the flagship for everything. For classification, extraction, and simple summarization the small model usually matches quality on a golden dataset at far lower cost.

sections.title: 3. Calling models: InvokeModel vs Converse vs streaming

keyTerms.definition: The original Bedrock runtime API with provider-specific request and response bodies, required for embeddings.
The newer unified Bedrock API with one request shape across providers, built-in tool use, guardrails, caching, and structured output.
The streaming variant of Converse that returns tokens as they are generated for chat UIs.
The async S3-based option with hours of latency at about half the price for non-interactive work.
The standalone API that applies guardrail filters to any text, including output from non-Bedrock models.

recall.question: Which API do you use for embeddings?
recall.answer: InvokeModel only. Converse is for text generation only and cannot do embeddings with any configuration.

recall.question: What is the classic Provisioned Throughput throttling bug?
recall.answer: Buying capacity but calling the base model ID instead of the provisioned model ARN, so traffic hits on-demand quotas. Buying more units cannot fix a routing bug.

recall.question: Why use streaming for a chat UI?
recall.answer: Users perceive a chat as fast when tokens start arriving in 300 milliseconds, even if the full answer takes 10 seconds.

sections.title: 4. Inference routing and pricing: profiles, routers, throughput

keyTerms.definition: Mechanisms that route a request to a model in another region for availability and failover, called with us., eu., apac., or global. prefixes.
A mechanism that routes each prompt to the cheapest model that can handle its complexity, optimizing cost versus quality.
Reserved model capacity bought per model unit per hour for 1 to 6 months, giving guaranteed throughput and stable latency.
A cost saver that bills repeated input prefixes at a reduced rate via cachePoint or cache_control, with a TTL.
Pay-per-token inference with no commitment, the default for spiky or experimental traffic.

recall.question: What is the one error tested by 'bought Provisioned Throughput but still throttled'?
recall.answer: The code calls the base model ID instead of the provisioned model ARN. Increasing model units does not fix routing.

recall.question: What is the hybrid capacity design for a 2M daily baseline plus 10x Friday spikes with sub-3s latency?
recall.answer: Provisioned Throughput for the predictable baseline and on-demand for spikes. Sizing PT for the peak wastes money on idle capacity.

recall.question: What problem does each of the three confused mechanisms solve?
recall.answer: Inference profiles solve availability across regions, prompt routers solve cost versus quality per prompt, and Provisioned Throughput solves guaranteed capacity.

sections.title: 5. The approach ladder: prompt, RAG, agents, fine-tuning

keyTerms.definition: The decision ladder for GenAI approaches: prompt engineering, RAG, agents, then fine-tuning, tried from cheapest to most expensive.
Changing the instructions and examples sent to the model without adding new knowledge or training.
Retrieval-Augmented Generation: looking up facts in your documents at answer time and citing them.
Training a small cheap student model to copy a big teacher model for one narrow task.
Retraining parts of the model on labeled data to bake a new behavior into its weights.

recall.question: What is the ladder rule?
recall.answer: Start at the lowest step that can work and climb only with proof that the lower step fails. The correct exam answer is the lowest step that meets all limits.

recall.question: Why is fine-tuning on company documents the exam's favorite wrong answer?
recall.answer: Retrained knowledge goes stale between cycles and cannot cite sources. When a scenario says documents update regularly or answers must cite sources, the answer is RAG.

recall.question: Which scenario verb maps to which rung?
recall.answer: Format or tone is prompt engineering, facts or citations is RAG, actions or tools is agents, and baked-in behavior at scale is fine-tuning.

sections.title: 6. PoC first, the GenAI Lens, and reusable components

keyTerms.definition: A small throwaway build on Bedrock using on-demand inference that validates feasibility, performance, and business value before any production commitment.
The AWS Well-Architected Framework Generative AI Lens, a published review checklist for GenAI workloads.
Build-once parts shared across deployments, such as prompt templates, model routing layers, guardrail policies, and evaluation harnesses.

recall.question: What three questions does a PoC answer?
recall.answer: Does it work, is it fast enough, and is it worth it.

recall.question: What is the correct chain for 12 languages, 99.9 percent availability with failover, model switching without code changes, and a CTO who wants validation?
recall.answer: PoC on Bedrock, cross-region inference for failover, and Lambda plus API Gateway for model switching.

recall.question: What is the nonsense distractor about the GenAI Lens?
recall.answer: 'Deploy the GenAI Lens.' The Lens is a review checklist, not a product you deploy.

sections.title: 7. Custom models: fine-tuning, continued pre-training, distillation, imports

keyTerms.definition: Supervised fine-tuning that trains the model on labeled prompt-and-response pairs to learn a behavior such as tone or classification.
Training further on unlabeled domain text such as manuals so the model absorbs domain vocabulary.
Training a small cheap student model to imitate a large teacher model on one narrow task.
Low-Rank Adaptation, a parameter-efficient method that trains only small weight deltas called adapters instead of all weights.
Models customized outside Bedrock and brought in, validated by Bedrock and served through Bedrock APIs.

recall.question: What is the master trap of the whole domain?
recall.answer: Fine-tuning for knowledge instead of behavior. Documents that change monthly point to RAG with a sync schedule, not fine-tuning.

recall.question: What does 'the customization job succeeded but calls fail' point to?
recall.answer: Missing Provisioned Throughput. Most custom models need it to be invocable, so the failure is not bad training data.

recall.question: When is distillation the correct answer?
recall.answer: Same narrow task millions of times where cost is the problem. You get teacher quality at student cost.

sections.title: 8. Swapping models without redeploys

keyTerms.definition: AWS AppConfig holds the model choice as runtime configuration, so changes apply in seconds without redeploying code.
A resilience pattern that trips after repeated model failures, routes to a fallback model or cached response, and probes before restoring.
The system getting cheaper and simpler under failure instead of dying, via fallback routing.

recall.question: What is the canonical trio for switching models without redeploys?
recall.answer: AppConfig holds the model choice, Lambda holds the routing logic and calls Converse, and API Gateway is the stable front door.

recall.question: Why does a CloudFormation parameter fail the no-redeploy constraint?
recall.answer: Changing a CloudFormation parameter redeploys the stack. EventBridge also fails because it routes events and holds no configuration.

recall.question: How does the circuit breaker provide graceful degradation?
recall.answer: It trips after repeated failures, routes to a fallback model or cached response, then probes the primary before switching back. The system gets simpler under failure instead of dying.

sections.title: 9. Data pipelines for FMs: validation, processing, extraction

keyTerms.definition: The service that processes documents, images, video, and audio into structured output with standard output or custom blueprints.
The service that runs automated data-quality rules and monitoring on pipeline outputs.
The service that converts audio to text, supporting speaker diarization and custom vocabularies for domain terms.
The service that extracts entities, detects language, and detects PII in text.
Checking incoming data for completeness and sanity before it reaches a model or knowledge base.

recall.question: What is the correct chain for ingesting 10,000 mixed files a day into structured summaries?
recall.answer: Bedrock Data Automation with blueprints for extraction, S3 versioning for traceability, Lambda for validation, and Glue Data Quality plus CloudWatch for monitoring.

recall.question: What are the two big traps in data pipelines?
recall.answer: Bedrock Guardrails do not extract content; they are safety filters. Amazon Kendra is enterprise search, not a knowledge base; generated answers with citations need Knowledge Bases.

recall.question: Which service does which job in a multimodal ingestion pipeline?
recall.answer: BDA extracts, Lambda validates and normalizes, Glue Data Quality plus CloudWatch monitor, and Transcribe handles audio.

sections.title: 10. Chunking strategies

keyTerms.definition: Splitting documents into retrievable pieces that each become one vector for retrieval.
Chunking that splits every N tokens with an overlap percentage, predictable and cheap and best for uniform text like FAQs.
Matching precisely on child chunks while giving the model the parent chunk for section context.
Cutting where meaning changes by analyzing sentence and topic boundaries, the best quality but slower and more expensive at ingestion.
Keeping the last X percent of a chunk as the start of the next so boundary sentences appear whole.

recall.question: What is the answer when retrieval misses answers spanning section boundaries in product manuals?
recall.answer: Hierarchical chunking. Increasing embedding dimensions does not fix split context, and switching the generation model does not fix it either.

recall.question: Why is chunking set at data-source creation?
recall.answer: Changing the strategy requires recreating the data source and re-ingesting. 'Just change the chunking' is never a quick fix.

recall.question: What is the worked overlap example?
recall.answer: 500-token chunks with 20 percent overlap give 400 new tokens per chunk, so a 2,000-token parent needs 5 chunks. At 40 percent overlap it needs about 7.

sections.title: 11. Embeddings: Titan Embeddings and Cohere Embed

keyTerms.definition: A list of numbers forming a vector that represents a piece of text, so similar meanings sit close together in space.
The angle between two embedding vectors, where a smaller angle means closer meaning.
The cheap default embedding model with configurable dimensions of 1024, 512, or 256.
The embedding model with multilingual strength and an input_type parameter distinguishing queries from documents.
The Cohere parameter that embeds queries and documents with different prefixes, where the wrong type degrades match quality.

recall.question: Which API do embedding calls use?
recall.answer: InvokeModel. Converse is for text generation only and cannot produce embeddings.

recall.question: What happens if you switch the embedding model without re-embedding?
recall.answer: Retrieval quality collapses because stored vectors come from the old model's vector space while queries use the new one. A model swap means full re-ingestion.

recall.question: What is the dimension trade-off?
recall.answer: Dropping from 1024 to 256 cuts vector storage to one quarter and speeds up search. The accuracy cost is measured on a golden dataset.

sections.title: 12. Vector stores compared

keyTerms.definition: A store, also called a vector database, that holds embeddings and finds the nearest ones to a query embedding fast.
The managed scalable default vector store for large-scale AWS-native vector search.
The option that keeps vectors alongside relational data in Postgres, combining SQL filters with vector similarity in one query.
The cheap S3-native vector store with zero cluster management, best for prototypes and small workloads.
The graph database for multi-hop relationship traversal in GraphRAG, not for plain document similarity search.

recall.question: Which store for an app already on Aurora PostgreSQL that needs similar-ticket search filtered by customer?
recall.answer: Aurora pgvector. One database holds tables and embeddings, so a single query combines the customer filter with vector similarity.

recall.question: What are the classic wrong-store traps?
recall.answer: ElastiCache as durable vector storage, DynamoDB as a vector similarity engine, and Neptune for plain document RAG. ElastiCache is a cache, DynamoDB is not a vector store, and Neptune is only for graph traversal.

recall.question: When is Neptune the correct answer?
recall.answer: Only when the scenario mentions relationships or multi-hop traversal, such as fraud rings. For plain similarity search it is the expensive wrong choice.

sections.title: 13. Knowledge Bases: the managed RAG service

keyTerms.definition: The fully managed RAG service that chunks, embeds, and indexes documents so you point at documents and get a queryable RAG backend.
The API that retrieves relevant chunks and returns a model-generated answer with source citations.
The configuration that picks up new and changed documents automatically, from one-time to scheduled or on-demand.
A connected S3 bucket, web crawler, Confluence, SharePoint, or Salesforce that the knowledge base ingests and syncs.

recall.question: What is the default exam answer for private documents with citations and minimal operational overhead?
recall.answer: Bedrock Knowledge Bases with an S3 data source, a scheduled sync, and RetrieveAndGenerate. Hand-rolled RAG is a distractor.

recall.question: What is the multi-tenant trap?
recall.answer: One shared knowledge base with prompt instructions like 'only answer about your own hotel.' Prompt-level filtering is not a security boundary, so use separate knowledge bases per tenant with IAM.

recall.question: Why can't chunking be changed in place?
recall.answer: Chunking is set per data source at creation. Changing it requires recreating the data source and re-ingesting.

sections.title: 14. RAG end to end

keyTerms.definition: Retrieval-Augmented Generation, the pattern where the model answers from retrieved passages at query time instead of its training weights alone.
The managed call that builds a prompt from the question plus retrieved chunks and returns a cited answer.
Whether the model actually uses the retrieved context, the generation-stage check when chunks are relevant but answers are wrong.
The date where a foundation model's training data ends, so it knows nothing about newer private documents.

recall.question: What are the five stages of the RAG loop?
recall.answer: Ingest, chunk and embed, store, retrieve, and generate.

recall.question: When RAG returns confident but wrong answers and the retrieved chunks look relevant, what is the fix?
recall.answer: It is a grounding problem, not a retrieval problem. Strengthen instructions, grounding checks, or structured output instead of changing the embedding or generation model.

recall.question: Why does RAG beat fine-tuning for documents that change monthly?
recall.answer: New documents become searchable after the next sync with no retraining, and answers can cite sources. Fine-tuning would need monthly retraining and cannot cite sources.

sections.title: 15. Retrieval quality: hybrid search, rerank, query handling, debugging

keyTerms.definition: Combining vector search with keyword search so exact terms like product codes are not lost to pure semantic matching.
A second scoring pass where a dedicated rerank model reorders first-pass candidates into a better-ordered top-K.
Rewriting the user's question before retrieval by adding synonyms and related terms.
Splitting a complex multi-part question into 2 to 4 sub-queries, each retrieved separately.
The classic keyword-scoring algorithm used for the lexical signal in hybrid search.

recall.question: What is the correct debug order when RAG answers are wrong?
recall.answer: Check retrieval relevance, then chunking, then embeddings, then grounding. Fix the earliest failing stage and never change the generation model first.

recall.question: What is the full quality pipeline for exact SKUs plus vague questions that must return the 5 best passages?
recall.answer: Query handling expands or decomposes the query, hybrid search fuses vector and keyword candidates, and a rerank model scores the fused list down to a final top-K.

recall.question: Why is reranking economical?
recall.answer: The expensive scoring runs on tens of candidates, not the whole index. A common setup retrieves 50 candidates and reranks down to 5 for generation.

sections.title: 16. Prompt Management, Prompt Flows, and prompt governance

keyTerms.definition: Bedrock's managed treatment of prompts as versioned resources with {{variable}} placeholders, immutable versions, and A/B variants.
The visual no-code builder for multi-step GenAI workflows with prompt, agent, knowledge base, Lambda, and condition nodes.
Alternative versions of a prompt run against each other on live traffic for A/B testing.
Immutable snapshots of a prompt where publishing a new version never changes an old one, so rollback is exact.

recall.question: What is the answer for 15 prompts where marketing keeps changing tone and no redeploys are allowed?
recall.answer: Prompt Management with versions and variants. Bedrock Agents is the distractor because agents are for dynamic tool-using reasoning, not static prompt storage.

recall.question: When do you use Prompt Flows versus Step Functions?
recall.answer: Prompt Flows for a fixed deterministic multi-step chain built by non-engineers. Step Functions when the workflow needs human approvals, waits, and timeouts.

recall.question: What distinguishes prompt versions from variants?
recall.answer: Versions are immutable releases that enable exact rollback. Variants are alternative versions run against each other for A/B testing.

sections.title: 17. Data privacy and compliance in Bedrock

keyTerms.definition: The service that finds PII at scale in S3 by scanning buckets and flagging sensitive data before it reaches a model.
The service that detects PII entities in text in real time, finding more than 30 entity types.
Bedrock Guardrails sensitive-information filters that block or mask PII at inference time in both directions.
PrivateLink endpoints for Bedrock services that keep API traffic off the public internet with no NAT gateway needed.
The encryption service for invocation logs and stored data in compliance-heavy environments.

recall.question: What is the select-three PII pipeline for customer-service GenAI with minimal custom work?
recall.answer: Macie to discover PII in S3, Comprehend for real-time PII detection in text, and Bedrock Guardrails sensitive-information filters at inference.

recall.question: What are the PII distractor traps?
recall.answer: Translate for PII obfuscation, because translation preserves meaning and protects nothing. Rekognition for text PII, because Rekognition is a vision service.

recall.question: What does the exam want for invocation logging in a healthcare scenario?
recall.answer: KMS encryption of the log destination and bounded retention, or disabled logging. Logs contain the PII you protect.

sections.title: 18. Model Evaluation Basics

keyTerms.definition: Cheap repeatable benchmarks using built-in or custom datasets with computed metrics like accuracy, stability, and toxicity.
Using a model to grade outputs on correctness, completeness, faithfulness, harmfulness, refusal, and style at scale.
Human raters scoring subjective dimensions like voice and taste, the most expensive and slowest option at scale.
Whether the retrieved chunks support every claim the model makes, scored separately from retrieval relevance.
Serving a new version to a small slice of traffic, typically 1 to 5 percent, before full rollout.

recall.question: What is the correct evaluation for comparing two models on summarization quality including brand voice at scale?
recall.answer: LLM-as-a-judge for scale plus human evaluation for brand voice. Programmatic metrics cannot judge voice and human review alone does not scale.

recall.question: What do retrieval relevance and faithfulness measure in RAG evaluation?
recall.answer: Retrieval relevance asks if retrieval found the right chunks. Faithfulness asks if the chunks support every claim.

recall.question: What is the correct drift detection design with minimal custom work?
recall.answer: Scheduled Bedrock evaluation jobs plus CloudWatch anomaly detection on token metrics. A hand-built Glue and Athena pipeline is maximum custom work.

sections.title: Exam Drill: Questions Per Topic

keyTerms.definition: A mechanism that routes a request to a model in another region for availability and failover.
Training a small cheap student model to imitate a large teacher model on one narrow task.
Bedrock's managed treatment of prompts as versioned resources with immutable versions and A/B variants.
Retrieval-Augmented Generation, the pattern where the model answers from retrieved passages at query time.
The standalone API that applies guardrail filters to any text, including traffic to and from non-Bedrock models.

recall.question: What is the correct design for a bank loan assistant that needs monthly manual citations, live API status checks, 20-minute conversation context, and minimal cost?
recall.answer: RAG with the manual for citations, a Bedrock Agent with an action group for the status API, and agent session memory. Each constraint maps to one rung.

recall.question: What is the correct fix when a RAG system misses numeric answers because table rows are split across chunks?
recall.answer: Advanced parsing for tables plus hierarchical chunking. The failure is at ingestion, so switching the generation model cannot help.

recall.question: What is the correct privacy architecture for a bank handling account numbers in chat with minimal custom code?
recall.answer: A Comprehend pre-filter to mask PII before prompt construction, VPC endpoints for Bedrock traffic, Guardrails on inputs and outputs, and KMS-encrypted invocation logs with a retention policy.
